title: THC Advanced Environment and Lighting
description: Advanced Environment and Lighting prepares experienced cultivation learners to verify environmental and lighting data quality, map spatial gradients, interpret airflow and heat/moisture loads, distinguish sensor faults from true crop conditions, evaluate PPFD/DLI and light distribution, and design evidence-based verification steps before recommending environmental or lighting changes.
intendedAudience: Cultivation Technician II and senior cultivation technicians
Cultivation staff responsible for sensor verification, environmental trend review, PPFD mapping or lighting checks
Learners progressing toward cultivation lead or specialist pathways
prerequisites: THC Cultivation Foundations or equivalent plant-environment knowledge is recommended.
Learners should be able to interpret temperature, RH, VPD, PPFD and DLI terminology and basic trend data.
Technician I-level measurement, documentation and workplace-safety competency is recommended before supervised practical work.
learningOutcomes: Design and evaluate a spatial environmental-sensor map that distinguishes representative crop conditions from controller-wall or single-point readings.
Assess sensor placement, calibration history, shielding, cross-sensor agreement and response behavior before concluding that a crop-space deviation is real.
Interpret airflow and canopy microclimate evidence to distinguish mixing problems, local dead zones and biologically excessive airflow.
Interpret sensible and latent loads, irrigation events, crop transpiration and control sequencing when evaluating environmental-capacity problems.
Compare lighting treatments using PPFD, DLI, spectral distribution, photoperiod, cultivar, stage and production goal rather than fixture marketing labels.
Build and interpret canopy PPFD maps using average, minimum, maximum and spatial variability rather than a single center measurement.
Evaluate whether fixture placement, canopy architecture or supplemental/interlighting changes are justified by measured spatial light distribution.
Evaluate UV or altered-photoperiod trials using documented dose, timing, wavelength, DLI and safety controls while preserving evidence limits.
Separate measurement fault, equipment fault, environmental-control fault and crop-response evidence before recommending corrective action.
Create a supervisor-ready environment/lighting verification report with measurements, source data, hypotheses, confidence limits, next checks and escalation boundaries.
evidencePolicy: Course claims should use cannabis-specific peer-reviewed evidence when available and established controlled-environment horticulture or plant-physiology evidence for general mechanisms. Every recommendation must distinguish measured fact from interpretation, and cultivar-, fixture-, room- or study-specific outcomes must not be presented as universal recipes. Sensor and light measurements require documented units, device/context, position, time and relevant calibration or verification status.
assessmentPolicy: Instruction uses mapped data sets, troubleshooting cases, PPFD/environment maps, sensor-verification exercises and evidence-based decision scenarios. Module checks are formative. The final credential assessment remains fail-closed until adequate bank depth, human review, accessibility review, pilot evidence and standard-setting are complete. Practical performance should include sensor/data-quality verification and canopy light mapping with a documented technical handoff.

practicalEvidenceRequirements: annotated environmental trend or spatial map
top/mid-canopy PPFD map with uniformity analysis
extensions.roleBoundary: Technician II may verify measurements, identify probable sensor/equipment/data-quality faults, perform approved checks, compare measured light/environment conditions to work instructions and recommend next verification or escalation. The learner does not gain unrestricted authority to redesign facility HVAC/electrical systems, bypass safety controls or make unapproved program changes.
extensions.credentialStatement: Successful completion may contribute to the THC Advanced Environment and Lighting certificate when all assessment, practical, review, identity, issuance and release requirements are active. The credential documents educational/workforce achievement and is not a government license or independent personnel certification.
productionActivationRequirements: Add and validate sufficient randomized final-assessment bank depth across all six objectives.
Add a dedicated lighting/environment performance assessment or map equivalent evidence to an approved integrated practical.
Record human SME and assessment review.
Run learner pilot and item-analysis review.
Verify source freshness and public learner rendering.
Verify credential identity, issuance and public-verification flow.
